screening.title: Screen before publishing
screening.disclaimer: These are creative suggestions, not cleared names. The tool does not guarantee availability — work through the checklist before you commit to any candidate.

items.title: Search the exact name
items.description: Search the full pen name in a search engine with quotes around it. If a well-known author or brand already owns it, cross the candidate off.

items.title: Check author databases and retailers
items.description: Look the name up on book retailer author pages and library catalogs. You are checking for existing authors publishing under it, not just exact duplicates.

items.title: Check domains and social handles
items.description: See whether a matching website domain and the social handles you would want are already taken by someone active in your niche.

items.title: Search the relevant trademark databases
items.description: Search trademark registries that apply to your market — for example USPTO or EUIPO, plus your local registry — for the name in publishing-related classes.

items.title: Review contracts, tax, and professional advice
items.description: Before signing anything, read how your publisher handles pen names and get advice on taxes, banking, and any professional rules that apply to writing under a pseudonym.

feature1.name: feature_intro
feature1.label: Overview
feature1.title: What This Pen Name Generator Is Good At
feature1.description: Built for authors who need a byline that fits their shelf — invented fresh for your genre and goals, never recycled from a list.

items.title: Genre-aware candidates
items.description: A romance byline and a hard sci-fi byline should not sound alike. The genre control shapes rhythm, initials, and surname style for the shelf you write for.

items.title: Pronunciation for every name
items.description: Each candidate ships with a simple syllable guide, so you can say it at signings, interviews, and podcasts before you commit.

items.title: Reasons, not just names
items.description: Every candidate explains why it works as a byline — what it signals to readers, retailers, and reviewers in your genre.

how_to_use.name: how_to_use
how_to_use.label: HOW TO USE
how_to_use.title: How to Use the Pen Name Generator in 3 Steps
how_to_use.description: The pen name generator takes you from blank page to a shortlist of usable bylines in under a minute.

items.title: Set genre, goals, and market
items.description: Pick the genre you write in, what the name is for — one brand, genre separation, or privacy — and the market your readers buy in.

items.title: Generate and compare ten candidates
items.description: Read the pronunciation and reason on each card, favorite the ones that click, and add a cue like a sound you love for sharper results.

items.title: Screen your favorite before publishing
items.description: Run your shortlist through the five-step screening checklist, then copy the winner into your manuscript and accounts.

feature2.name: feature_benefits
feature2.label: Benefits
feature2.title: Why the Right Pen Name Matters
feature2.description: A pen name is a publishing decision, not just a label. The right one works everywhere your books live.

items.title: One byline, one brand
items.description: Readers follow names they recognize. A coherent byline builds series loyalty, mailing-list trust, and shelf presence across books.

items.title: Room for genre switches
items.description: Writing cozy romance and gritty thrillers? Separate pen names keep both audiences from bouncing off covers that promise the wrong genre.

items.title: Distance by design
items.description: A chosen byline keeps your legal name off covers, catalogs, and search results — one layer of separation you control as a public author.

feature3.name: use_cases
feature3.label: Use Cases
feature3.title: Who Uses the Pen Name Generator
feature3.description: Writers who need a professional byline without a naming committee.

items.title: Debut novelists
items.description: Test-drive bylines that read well on a cover, a spine, and a review before your first book goes out under it.

items.title: Multi-genre indies
items.description: Spin up a distinct, genre-appropriate byline for each pen-name line you publish, then keep them separate in retailer metadata.

items.title: Privacy-conscious professionals
items.description: Teachers, lawyers, and civil servants who write fiction keep their day identity off the byline while staying pronounceable at events.

items.title: Why do authors use pen names?
items.description: Authors write under pen names to keep one brand per genre, to separate public and private life, to avoid a name collision with an existing author, or simply because a chosen byline reads better on a cover than a legal name.

items.title: Does the tool check whether a pen name is free to use?
items.description: No. The generator does not guarantee availability and does not check registries, retailers, domains, or trademarks. Treat every candidate as a creative suggestion and screen it with the five-step checklist before you publish under it.

items.title: Will a pen name keep me anonymous?
items.description: A pen name does not automatically make you anonymous. Contracts, copyright filings, taxes, and metadata can still connect a byline to your legal identity. If anonymity matters, get professional advice on how pseudonyms are handled in your publishing contracts and jurisdiction.

items.title: Can I use different pen names for different genres?
items.description: Yes — that is what the 'Separate names per genre' brand goal is for. Many authors run one byline per genre so readers always know what a cover promises. Keep each line consistent in retailer metadata and on your covers.

items.title: How do I screen a candidate before committing?
items.description: Search the exact name in quotes, check author pages on retailers, look at domain and social handles, search the trademark registries for your market, and read the pen-name clauses in your publishing contract. The five-step checklist on this page walks you through it.

items.title: Why doesn't the tool suggest names based on gender or ethnicity?
items.description: Bylines are judged as bylines. The generator never claims or implies anything about the gender, ethnicity, nationality, religion, or cultural identity behind a name — it suggests names purely by how they read in your genre and market.

items.title: Can I trademark or register a generated pen name?
items.description: Sometimes, but the tool makes no claim about it. Registration depends on your jurisdiction, the classes you file in, and existing marks. Screen candidates in the relevant trademark databases and consult a professional before filing anything.
